comparator.name: Bachelor Psychology, Track Psychopathology, Health and Prevention
comparator.sourceNotes: Reconstructed from VU Amsterdam's current official sources for the Fall-2026 cohort: the Faculty of Behavioural and Movement Sciences' Teaching and Examination Regulations for the Bachelor's programme Psychology (CROHO 56604), academic year 2026-2027, and VU's current Dutch-language 'Bachelor Psychologie' overview and 'Inhoud' (content) pages. Article 10.2 of the TER confirms the programme has exactly two tracks under this one shared registration -- a Dutch track (described in a separate Dutch-language OER) and an International track (described in this TER, taught in English) -- and Article 7.1 confirms both share the same CROHO 56604 registration. The normalized target cp-000114 records languages_json=["NLD"], i.e. the Dutch-track registration of this shared programme. The compulsory academic core (Years 1-2) and the Year-3 elective/major structure that the TER documents for the International track are the same university-wide courses taught to Dutch-track students in Dutch: VU's Dutch-language 'Inhoud' page independently lists directly corresponding Dutch course titles for every TER-listed compulsory course (Inleiding Psychologie/Introduction to Psychology, Sociale Psychologie/Social Psychology, Ontwikkelingspsychologie en Psychopathologie/Developmental Psychology and Psychopathology, Meten en Diagnostiek 1-2/Measurement Theory and Assessment 1-2, Methodologie 1-2/Research Methods 1-2, Statistiek 1-2/Statistics 1-2, Filosofie en Psychologie/Philosophy and Psychology, Arbeids- en Organisatiepsychologie/Work and Organizational Psychology, Samenspel van Genen en Omgeving/Genetic and Environmental Interaction, Neuropsychologie/Neuropsychology, Big Data in Psychology, Psychologische Gespreksvaardigheden 1-2/Psychological Communication Skills 1-2), so the current TER is used as the source of record for exact EC and structure, cross-verified by the Dutch overview page. Year 1 (Article 11.3, 60 EC, all compulsory): Introduction to Psychology (P_BINLPSY, 6), Research Methods 1 (P_BMETHOD_1, 6), Statistics 1 (P_BSTATIS_1, 6), Biological and Cognitive Psychology (P_BBIOCOG, 9), Big Data in Psychology (P_BETBDAT, 3), Measurement Theory and Assessment 1 (P_BMETDIA_1, 6), Developmental Psychology and Psychopathology (P_BOWPSY, 9), Social Psychology (P_BSOCPSY, 6), Personality Theory and Assessment (P_BPERSON, 6), Psychological Communication Skills 1: Basic Skills (P_BPSG1BA, 3). Year 2 (Article 11.3, 48 EC compulsory + Article 11.4.1, 12 EC preminor, 60 EC total): Neuropsychology (P_BNEUROP, 6), Philosophy and Psychology (P_BFILPSY, 6), Measurement Theory and Assessment 2 (P_BMETDIA_2, 6), Work and Organizational Psychology (P_BARORPS, 9), Psychological Communication Skills 2: Professional Skills (P_BPSG2PV, 3), Genetic and Environmental Interaction (P_BSAGEOM, 6), Statistics 2 (P_BSTATIS_2, 6), Research Methods 2 (P_BMETHOD_2, 6); Article 11.4.1 requires choosing one of three connected preminor pairs, each worth 12 EC across two parts -- no target-specific evidence favours one pair, so the first-listed pair in the TER's own Article 11.4.1 table is used as the neutral tie-break: Behaviour and the Brain part 1: Addiction (P_BBAA_1, 6) and part 2: Cognitive Neuroscience (P_BBAC_2, 6). Year 3 (Article 11.4.2 and Article 12, 60 EC): Article 12.1 fixes the first semester as at least 30 EC of elective units of education, taken either as a minor or as an individually chosen package with at least 12 EC at level 300; Article 11.4.2 notes that students generally take both the minor and the second-semester subjects from the same chosen track, so the minor named for the selected track in Article 12.2 is used to instantiate this elective space rather than leaving it a wholly generic blank: Minor Psychopathology, Health and Prevention (30 EC): Basic Assessment and Coaching Skills (6), Diversity in Clinical Practice (6), Psychopathology and Prevention (6), Research Tool Kit: Epidemiology (6), Psychopharmacology (6). Article 11.4.2's own Year-3 table then lists the compulsory and elective track-specific units for the chosen Track Psychopathology, Health and Prevention (30 EC): Low Intensity Treatments for Common Mental Health Problems (P_BKPSIN, 6), Statistics 3 (P_BSTAT3KL, 6), B-thesis (P_BTHESEKLI, 12), and one suggested elective chosen from four (Cognition and Emotion, Cooperation and Competition, Neuropsychology of Ageing, Psychological Interventions for Complex Problems); no target-specific evidence favours one, so the first-listed option in the TER's own Article 11.4.2 table is used as the neutral tie-break, Cognition and Emotion (P_BCOGNEM, 6). Article 9.1 requires all Year-1 components to be passed before the B-thesis may begin. 60 (Year 1) + 60 (Year 2) + 60 (Year 3) = 180 EC. No further official source needed to be consulted: the TER and the Dutch overview/content pages together establish a complete, internally consistent, entirely accounted-for 180-EC pathway with explicit EC and compulsory/elective status for every component, and explicit, UCR-independent tie-break judgments (preminor pair, track choice and suggested elective) fixed before any UCR course was considered.

routeSelection.basis: Registry row 122 (source_provider_id 111A136, recognized_programme_code 56604) records languages_json=["NLD"] for cp-000114, i.e. this normalized target is the Dutch-track registration of VU's shared Bachelor Psychology programme; TER Article 10.2 confirms the programme's Dutch track and International track share one CROHO 56604 registration but are separately documented (the Dutch track in a separate Dutch-language OER not retrievable through available tools; the International track in this TER). Within either track, Article 11.4.2 requires every student to choose one of several formal Year-3 tracks before the pathway can be instantiated, and the normalized target itself names no specific one of these tracks. Applying Section 2.1's neutral hierarchy: no single track is clearly more representative of the whole degree's academic identity than the others, so the least specialised/most general available track is used. Of the four official tracks (Klinische Leerlijn; Psychopathology, Health and Prevention; Social and Organizational Psychology; Genes, Cognition and Behaviour), Track Psychopathology, Health and Prevention is the only one that is explicitly framed, in its own current official learning outcomes, as synthesising multiple perspectives (developmental, clinical and neuropsychological) on its subject rather than committing to one narrow professional lens (Klinische Leerlijn's own GZ-oriented clinical-intervention training), one applied domain (Social and Organizational Psychology's organisational/HR focus) or one biomedical specialism (Genes, Cognition and Behaviour's genetics/neuroscience focus); it is therefore the least specialised of the four under the current official learning-outcome descriptions. It is also the only one of the three tracks open to non-Klinische-Leerlijn students that is fully documented in currently retrievable current official evidence for the 2026-2027 academic year (Klinische Leerlijn's own curriculum is confirmed by this TER to exist only in a separate Dutch-language OER that public tools could not retrieve). This choice was not made because it produces an easier UCR match: at the time of route selection no UCR course content had yet been considered.

core: Understanding why people think, feel and behave as they do, and how thoughts, emotions and social relationships shape behaviour
Clinical psychology: understanding mental health problems and helping people recover
Psychopathology, health and prevention from a developmental, clinical and neuropsychological perspective
The brain, cognition and behaviour, including biological and cognitive psychology and neuropsychology
Child and adolescent development and lifespan developmental psychology
How genes and environment interact in shaping behaviour and psychological disease
Statistics and quantitative and qualitative psychological research methods
Observing, analysing and experimentally studying behaviour, including designing experiments and measuring brain activity
Professional communication skills: confidential interviewing, active listening and asking effective questions
Neuropsychology: the neural mechanisms behind perception, action and cognition
adjacent: Social influence, groups and social media
Motivation, work and organisational psychology, including social and organisational psychology as a named study direction
questions: Illustrative questions the programme uses to introduce psychology to prospective students (why people repeatedly check their phones, how TikTok trends influence choices, whether genes contribute to ADHD or addiction, how young people become mentally resilient, preventing online addiction, helping people with anxiety or trauma, why healthy behaviour relapses)

Further-study and career trajectories the programme prepares graduates for (research-master specialisations in clinical/developmental psychopathology, cognitive neuropsychology and genes in behaviour and health; work and organisational psychology careers; behaviour-change campaigns; UX and market research; health and wellbeing projects; research assistance; coaching)

alternatives.label: Psychopathology, Health and Clinical Psychology: A Developmental and Biological Approach
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum is dominated by a psychology-and-clinical cluster (7 of 24: Social Psychology, Statistics & Experimental Methods, Abnormal Psychology, Psychodiagnostics & Psychotherapies, Advanced Research Seminar, Lifespan Developmental Psychology, Youth Resilience to Extremism) and a biological/health cluster reproducing the track's own biomedical and neuropsychological content (7 of 24: Introduction to Brain & Behavior, Foundation of Life Health & Biomedicine, Neurobiology, Perception & Action, Higher Order Functions, Pharmacology, Mechanisms of Disease, Epidemiology & Public Health -- eight items reduced by one shared count), a methods/statistics cluster (4 of 24: Research Methods & Statistics, Introduction to Data Science, Machine Learning, Qualitative Research Methodology), a philosophy/ethics pairing (2 of 24: Philosophy of Mind, Ethics), one sociology course, one communication-skills course and Personal & Professional Development. The label names psychopathology, health and clinical psychology with a developmental and biological approach because the curriculum reproduces, across psychology, neuroscience and biomedical science, the track's own developmental-clinical-neuropsychological combination of compulsory and minor content, without foregrounding any single one of those strands as the whole programme.
alternatives.concept: The closest feasible UCR response to VU's Track Psychopathology, Health and Prevention: a psychology programme centred on mental health, psychopathology and clinical assessment, studied from a developmental, clinical, neuropsychological and biomedical perspective, and grounded throughout in quantitative and qualitative research methods and statistics -- reproducing as closely as UCR's catalogue allows the track's own combination of abnormal psychology, developmental psychopathology, epidemiology-based prevention, psychopharmacology and clinical intervention training.
progression: HCBGATE102 (semester 1) and HCBGATE101 (semester 1) are formal prerequisites for every dependent course in this alternative (HCBCOGN212, HCBPSYC212, HCBPSYC312, HCBPSYC314, HCBPSYC313 and HCBCOGN311 require HCBGATE102; HCBBIOM311 and HCBBIOM313 require HCBGATE101) and are both scheduled in semester 1, before every course that depends on them. Personal & Professional Development is scheduled in semester 1, within Year 1. Introductory Year-1 courses (Statistics & Experimental Methods, Neurobiology, Social Psychology, Philosophy of Mind) are concentrated in semesters 1-2, and level-3 advanced work (Pharmacology, Higher Order Functions, Abnormal Psychology's companion Psychodiagnostics & Psychotherapies, Youth Resilience to Extremism, Lifespan Developmental Psychology, Advanced Research Seminar, Mechanisms of Disease) is concentrated in semesters 3-6. Where an advisory continuation exists in the course evidence, it is honoured: Neurobiology (semester 2) precedes the more advanced Higher Order Functions (semester 3), and Introduction to Data Science (semester 3) precedes the more advanced Machine Learning (semester 5). Every course is offered in its assigned semester under the fixed Fall 2026 cohort schedule.

alternatives.label: Social Influence, Motivation and Organisational Psychology
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum replaces the closest match's clinical and biomedical cluster with an organisational-and-social-influence cluster (4 of 24: Psychology of Organizations & Leadership, Behavioral Economics, Persuasive Communication, From T.V. to TikTok), while retaining the same shared psychological, biological, methods and communication core (20 of 24) that both alternatives share. The label names social influence, motivation and organisational psychology because organisational, economic and media-based social influence -- rather than the closest match's clinical-psychopathology depth -- is what this curriculum studies in genuine depth.
alternatives.concept: A genuinely different second UCR route evidenced by the generator-eligible programme-interest row specifically naming social and organisational psychology as a stable study direction (row 5213), supported by target-specific evidence on social influence and social media (row 5207), motivation at work and in organisations (row 5209) and consumer behaviour and decision-making (row 5210): a concentration studying how individual and group behaviour is shaped, motivated and persuaded in organisational, economic and media settings, replacing the closest match's clinical-biomedical depth with organisational psychology, behavioral economics and communication/media studies.
progression: HCBGATE102 (semester 1) is a formal prerequisite for HCBCOGN212, HCBPSYC212, HCBPSYC314, HCBPSYC313 and HCBCOGN311, and is scheduled in semester 1, before every course that depends on it. BENGATE102 (semester 2) is a formal prerequisite for BENLEAD311 (semester 3) and BENECON314 (semester 6), each scheduled after it. Personal & Professional Development is scheduled in semester 1, within Year 1. Introductory Year-1 courses are concentrated in semesters 1-2, and level-3 advanced work (Higher Order Functions, Persuasive Communication, Psychology of Organizations & Leadership, Lifespan Developmental Psychology, Advanced Research Seminar, Behavioral Economics) is concentrated in semesters 3-6. Where an advisory continuation exists, it is honoured: Neurobiology (semester 2) precedes the more advanced Higher Order Functions (semester 3), and Introduction to Data Science (semester 3) precedes the more advanced Machine Learning (semester 5). Every course is offered in its assigned semester under the fixed Fall 2026 cohort schedule.
alternatives.distinctness: VU's Bachelor Psychology requires every student to take the same 108-EC compulsory academic core across psychology, biology, methods and communication skills before choosing one of four Year-3 tracks; the closest match reproduces the Track Psychopathology, Health and Prevention track's own clinical-biomedical depth in full. This alternative instead deepens a different, evidence-backed part of the same shared field -- how behaviour is shaped, motivated and persuaded in organisational, economic and media settings, matching VU's own Social and Organizational Psychology track -- rather than cosmetically relabelling the closest match. It replaces the closest match's Pharmacology, Mechanisms of Disease, Psychodiagnostics & Psychotherapies and Youth Resilience to Extremism (4 of 24 courses, 30 EC) with Psychology of Organizations & Leadership, Behavioral Economics, Persuasive Communication and From T.V. to TikTok (4 of 24 courses, 30 EC). This is a material curricular consequence, not cosmetic reshuffling: it changes the alternative's academic priorities from clinical-biomedical depth to an organisational, economic and media-based social-influence concentration, and the two alternatives share 20 of 24 courses while differing in 4 of 24 each way (30 EC), meeting the pairwise 30-EC/4-course minimum.

candidates.label: Social Influence, Motivation and Organisational Psychology

selection.assessment: The closest match directly owns fifteen generator-eligible rows: understanding why people think, feel and behave as they do and understanding/changing human behaviour (5203, 5204); mental health and helping people recover (5205); the brain, cognition and behaviour (5206); child and adolescent development (5208); clinical psychology as a stable study direction (5211); psychopathology, health and prevention as a stable study direction naming the chosen track itself (5212); biological and cognitive psychology (5215); how genes and environment interact (5220); psychological measurement and diagnosis (5221); statistics and psychological research methods (5223); observing and analysing behaviour and designing experiments and measuring brain activity (5224, 5226); interviewing, active listening and asking effective questions (5225); and stress, emotion and coping (5227). The remaining four generator-eligible rows -- social influence, groups and social media (5207), motivation at work and in organisations (5209), consumer behaviour and decision-making (5210), and social and organisational psychology as a stable study direction (5213) -- were independently assessed as one coherent candidate direction, 'Social Influence, Motivation and Organisational Psychology', additionally supported by the curricular-topic row on work and organisational psychology (5218). This candidate passes all four gates: it is evidence-backed by four generator-eligible rows including a stable study direction naming exactly this territory; it has a clear organising logic (an organisational, economic and media-based social-influence concentration rather than the closest match's clinical-biomedical depth); it is substantively distinct, replacing 4 of 24 courses (30 EC) with organisational-psychology, behavioral-economics and communication/media content, materially changing the alternative's academic priorities; and it is mechanically feasible against the enriched course database, with 4 distinct courses (30 EC) each way against the closest match, meeting the pairwise 30-EC/4-course floor. Production therefore includes it as the second alternative. A third candidate, 'Genes, Cognition and Behaviour', generated by the remaining stable-study-direction row (5214) and supported by rows on the brain/cognition/behaviour, biological and cognitive psychology, neuropsychology and gene-environment interaction (5206, 5215, 5219, 5220), was then assessed and rejected as not-substantively-distinct: its supporting evidence is already substantively owned and instantiated by the closest match, which already schedules UCR's entire relevant biological-and-cognitive-neuroscience catalogue (Introduction to Brain & Behavior, Neurobiology, Perception & Action, Higher Order Functions) plus its biomedical-foundations chain (Foundation of Life Health & Biomedicine, Pharmacology, Mechanisms of Disease); UCR's course catalogue additionally contains no dedicated behavioural-genetics or genes-and-behaviour course, so a genuinely distinct genetics-and-cognition concentration cannot be built without either reusing the same biological/neuro courses already scheduled in the closest match (failing the pairwise distinctness floor against it) or importing generic life-science courses (Human Physiology, Biochemistry, Molecular Cell Biology) whose relevance to genes, cognition and behaviour is at best generic biological background rather than a specific disciplinary implementation of that direction. Because its own evidence is already substantively covered by the closest match and no genuinely different 24-course curriculum follows from it given UCR's actual course offerings, it is rejected as not-substantively-distinct rather than manufactured through arbitrary substitution, and production stops at two included alternatives.

notes.text: VU's Bachelor Psychology combines a dedicated Psychology major with compulsory training in psychometric measurement and assessment (Measurement Theory and Assessment 1 and 2), personality psychology, and track-specific applied clinical-assessment and coaching skills, taught within a single dedicated Psychology department across three years. At UCR, students can study comparable subject matter through a smaller dedicated Psychology catalogue in the Health, Cognition and Behavior cluster, supplemented by adjacent Biomedical Science, Data Science, Sociology and Philosophy coursework, but UCR's catalogue currently contains no dedicated psychometrics/assessment course, no personality-psychology course, and no applied clinical assessment-and-coaching-skills course comparable to the VU minor's own Basic Assessment and Coaching Skills or Diversity in Clinical Practice components.

The related alternative, Social Influence, Motivation and Organisational Psychology, approaches VU's own Social and Organizational Psychology track through UCR's Business & Entrepreneurship and Media, Culture & Communication departments rather than a dedicated organisational-psychology major. UCR students can study organisational behaviour, behavioral economics and persuasive/media-based social influence, but UCR does not offer VU's own Human Resource Management, Group Dynamics or Cooperation and Competition courses, or a dedicated Social and Organizational Psychology concentration with its own track-specific statistics and bachelor thesis.
